verdict.rationale: Make documents that API requests use user authentication tokens 'with the relevant scopes enabled', and it offers OAuth 2.0 client flows. Together these give scoped credentials an agent could use. The evidence is a single thin mention, though, with no detail on the scope catalog, per-agent token issuance, or least-privilege controls for the MCP server. Missing for 10: documented scope list and granularity, agent-specific credential issuance or rotation guidance, MCP-server credential scoping, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: All requests to the Make API require authentication with the user authentication token with the relevant scopes enabled.
To be able to start using OAuth 2.0, your app has to request a client on our side.
